scope: Exercise the real shared border style/width/color Inspector routes through Canvas, draft Save, Editor reload and explicit Publish for every editable non-root PARTIAL type; fix the Divider public-render precedence defect found by the lifecycle test.

initial_regression.result: FAIL; the new type matrix reached explicit public Publish and exposed the Divider renderer overriding the shared responsive borderColor with its decoration-profile default.
initial_regression.failure: divider published CSS retained rgb(148, 163, 184) instead of the Inspector-authored value

test_hardening: The first mobile extension attempted public CSS assertions while the same scenario had intentionally hidden all 44 elements on mobile. The fixture now restores mobile visibility through the real Inspector and explicit Publish before measuring mobile border CSS.

A later retry hit one 12-second Canvas locator timeout in the long shared scenario; the browser fixture now permits 30 seconds for actions, and the full final scenario completed without assertion or timeout failures.

fix.change: Keep the versioned decoration border as Divider defaults, then emit shared responsive styles last so Inspector-authored border width, style and color take precedence, matching Canvas behavior.

coverage: all 44 editable non-root PARTIAL types expose border.style/border.width/border.color through responsive.set with borderStyle/borderWidth/borderColor Page Model keys
Inspector-authored solid 2px node-specific borders reach Canvas computed CSS
draft Save stores all three responsive desktop fields while the public CSS remains byte-for-byte behaviorally unchanged
all three border controls survive Editor reload and retain their values
explicit Publish applies each border to the public renderer with the exact expected computed width, style and color
the Divider public renderer now preserves shared responsive border overrides over its specialized decoration defaults
mobile visibility is re-enabled through Inspector, Save and explicit Publish before mobile appearance assertions
all 44 nodes receive independent dashed 3px mobile borders; mobile Save and Editor reload preserve them while desktop publication remains unchanged
mobile Publish updates public mobile borders without changing desktop CSS
resetting mobile border style, width and color restores desktop inheritance; Undo restores the mobile color and Redo restores desktop inheritance
draft reset Save preserves published mobile borders until explicit Publish removes the mobile overrides and restores inherited desktop CSS
